body:
Almost every week someone asks us the same question: "Fifty thousand mein kaunsa phone loon?" Fair question — and honestly, a harder one than it looks. This is the price range where shops push whatever gives them margin, where two phones with the same sticker price can feel completely different in the hand, and where one wrong variant (the 4 GB model instead of the 8 GB) can ruin an otherwise good purchase.

The six phones below are all on sale in Pakistan now for under Rs 50,000, and they are not interchangeable. Each suits a different kind of buyer, and the differences — screen technology, chipset, charging speed — matter more than the small gaps in price. Prices are the market prices we track on Check Specs at the time of writing.

The six, side by side

PhonePriceDisplayChipsetMain cameraBattery
Tecno Spark 30 ProRs 41,499AMOLED, 120HzHelio G100108 MP5000 mAh, 33W
Infinix Hot 40 ProRs 44,999IPS LCD, 120HzHelio G99108 MP5000 mAh, 33W
Redmi 13Rs 44,999IPS LCD, 90HzHelio G91 Ultra108 MP5030 mAh, 33W
Vivo Y28Rs 46,999IPS LCD, 90HzHelio G8550 MP6000 mAh, 44W
Samsung Galaxy A07Rs 47,999PLS LCD, 90HzHelio G9950 MP5000 mAh, 25W
Infinix Note 50s 5GRs 49,999AMOLED, 144HzDimensity 7300 Ultimate64 MP5500 mAh, 45W

Start here: Tecno Spark 30 Pro (Rs 41,499)

If you just want one recommendation, take this one and keep the change. It is the cheapest phone on this page, and the screen is the reason it leads the list. An AMOLED panel with a 120Hz refresh rate and a manufacturer-rated peak brightness of 1,700 nits is well above what this price usually buys. The main camera is a 108 MP unit, the Helio G100 is a capable chipset for everyday applications, and 33W charging is included. Unless gaming or maximum battery life is the priority, this is the default recommendation here. Full specs and price.

The gamer's phone: Infinix Hot 40 Pro (Rs 44,999)

PUBG and COD Mobile players, this one is aimed at you. The Helio G99 is the chipset budget gaming phones keep coming back to, for good reason, and Infinix pairs it with a 120Hz screen and up to 12 GB of RAM. On paper, that combination should deliver noticeably smoother gameplay than the G85 and G91-class chips elsewhere in this list. The 32 MP selfie camera has its own dual-LED flash, a genuinely useful addition for video calls in poor light. The battery is 5,000 mAh with 33W charging — Infinix advertises 20% to 75% in 35 minutes — which makes short top-ups between sessions practical. Full specs and price.

Camera first: Redmi 13 (Rs 44,999)

A useful distinction for phone cameras in this range: the megapixel count is largely marketing, but autofocus is not. The Redmi 13's 108 MP main camera has PDAF, so it locks focus quickly instead of hunting, which makes a practical difference with moving subjects. The 5,030 mAh battery is sized to cover a full day of typical use, and there is a 256 GB variant if you shoot a lot of photos and video. The 90Hz screen is a step behind the 120Hz crowd, and storage is the slower eMMC type, so large app installs and file transfers take longer than on UFS-equipped rivals. For camera-first buyers, it remains the strongest option here. Full specs and price.

Two days, no charger: Vivo Y28 (Rs 46,999)

The Y28 carries a 6,000 mAh battery, the largest in this list by a wide margin, and charges at 44W, so even that large battery refills quickly. Buyers who routinely spend long hours away from a charger, such as delivery riders, drivers and field staff, are exactly who this specification is aimed at. The trade-offs are real: the Helio G85 is a modest chipset, and the 720p screen is not sharp. The calculation will suit many working buyers: endurance and charging speed over display quality. Full specs and price.

The safe pair of hands: Samsung Galaxy A07 (Rs 47,999)

Some buyers walk into the shop already knowing they want a Samsung, and nothing written here will change their mind. Good news: they no longer have to settle for a weak phone to get the badge. The A07 runs the same Helio G99 as the Hot 40 Pro, has a 90Hz display, a 50 MP main camera with autofocus, and storage up to 256 GB with a dedicated memory card slot. Charging is a slower 25W and you pay a few thousand extra for the name — but you also get Samsung's service centres in every major city, which is worth something when a screen breaks in year two. Full specs and price.

Spend the whole budget: Infinix Note 50s 5G (Rs 49,999)

Right at the top of the budget sits the fastest phone in this list by a clear margin. The Dimensity 7300 Ultimate is a 4 nm chip — a different league from everything above — the AMOLED screen runs at 144Hz, and the 5,500 mAh battery is rated for a full charge in about 60 minutes at 45W. It is also the only 5G phone in this list. Pakistan's 5G rollout is still a promise rather than a reality, so do not buy it for 5G alone; buy it because its chipset has the most headroom, and is the most likely here to still feel responsive in three years. Full specs and price.

Before you pay — three things shops won't tell you

Check the variant. Several of these phones come in 4, 6 and 8 GB RAM versions that look identical. The price quoted to you is often for the smallest one. Ask, then check the box.

PTA approval matters. Buy the officially approved version with a proper warranty. A slightly cheaper non-PTA or CPID unit can stop working on local networks, and it is nearly impossible to resell later.

Prices move. The prices above are the Pakistan market prices we track on Check Specs and they do change — sometimes within the same week. Check the phone's page here on the day you buy; if a shop is asking well above it, you have your bargaining number.

Still deciding? Browse the full list on our best phones under Rs 50,000 page, put any two phones head to head in the comparison tool, or read our guides to the best battery phones in Pakistan and the best smartphones under $200 if your priorities are more specific.
desc: Looking for the best phone under Rs 50,000 in Pakistan? Six picks with prices, displays, chipsets, cameras and batteries compared side by side — from the Tecno Spark 30 Pro to the 5G-ready Infinix Note 50s.
title: Best Phones Under Rs 50,000 in Pakistan (2026) — Top 6 Picks
Huawei Enjoy 100 Pro and Pro Max Price in Pakistan — One of Them Has an 8,800 mAh Battery
desc: Huawei's Enjoy 100 Pro and Enjoy 100 Pro Max are coming with OLED screens, Kirin chips and a huge 8,800 mAh battery on the Max. Here are the expected Pakistan prices, full specs and the one big catch.
body:
Huawei does not launch phones in Pakistan the way it used to, so when two new models start showing up in search, people understandably want to know two things: what do they cost here, and is there a catch? With the Enjoy 100 Pro and Enjoy 100 Pro Max, the short answers are "less than you would expect" and "yes — one, covered below".

Both phones were announced on 28 October 2026, with release expected in early November. They are not officially on sale in Pakistan yet, so the prices below are expected prices based on the international figures — treat them as your bargaining compass, not a shop sticker.

Expected prices in Pakistan

ModelExpected priceBatteryDisplay
Huawei Enjoy 100 ProRs 74,9996100 mAh, 40W6.7-inch OLED, 120Hz
Huawei Enjoy 100 Pro MaxRs 82,9998800 mAh, 40W6.84-inch OLED, 120Hz

The Pro Max is the interesting one

Its 8,800 mAh silicon-carbon battery is, at the time of writing, one of the largest fitted to a mainstream smartphone — most flagships sit between 5,000 and 5,500 mAh. Huawei claims the phone is also drop resistant up to 1.8 metres and carries an IP65 rating, which makes the Pro Max feel like a phone built for people who are hard on phones: long days outdoors, travel, work sites. The screen peaks at a frankly absurd 8,000 nits on paper, so sunlight legibility should not be a problem.

There are trade-offs, and they are worth knowing before you fall for the battery number. The Pro Max is heavy at 228 g, and that weight is noticeable in daily handling. Its selfie camera is only 8 MP, oddly worse than the cheaper Pro's 32 MP unit. And the Kirin 8020A chipset is a capable mid-range chip, not a flagship slayer.

The standard Pro covers most buyers

The Enjoy 100 Pro keeps most of what matters: the same Kirin 8020A chip, a 6.7-inch OLED screen at 120Hz, a 50 MP main camera with autofocus, a better 32 MP selfie camera and a still-large 6,100 mAh battery with 40W charging. It is lighter (192 g), slimmer, and expected to cost about Rs 8,000 less. Unless you specifically need the giant battery, this is the one to watch.

The software question

Both phones run HarmonyOS 7.0. That means no Google Play Store and no built-in Google apps; Huawei's own AppGallery and workarounds cover many popular apps, but banking apps, some Google services and a few local apps can be hit or miss. For a phone you plan to buy through unofficial channels in Pakistan, that software question matters more than any spec on this page. If your life runs on Google apps, think carefully. If it does not — and the battery tempts you — the Pro Max in particular is a genuinely unusual phone.

We will update this post when the phones actually land in Pakistani shops and real prices replace the expected ones. Full specifications: Enjoy 100 Pro · Enjoy 100 Pro Max.

Frequently asked questions

Are the Enjoy 100 Pro and Pro Max officially available in Pakistan?

Not at the time of writing. The prices in this article are expected prices converted from the international figures. Any units that reach Pakistani shops in the near term will be imports, so confirm the warranty terms before buying.

Do these phones have Google apps and the Play Store?

No. Both run HarmonyOS 7.0 without built-in Google services. Huawei's AppGallery covers many popular applications, but some Google and banking apps may not work as they do on a conventional Android phone.

Which one should I buy?

Based on the published specifications, the Pro Max only justifies its higher expected price if the 8,800 mAh battery and tougher build matter to you. The standard Pro offers the same chipset, a better selfie camera and a lower price.

title: Nokia Flip and Feature Phones in Pakistan (2026): 2360 Flip and 235 4G Prices
desc: People are searching for Nokia flip phones again — for parents, for a second SIM, for a phone that simply lasts. Here are the Nokia 2360 Flip and Nokia 235 4G prices in Pakistan and an honest guide to who should buy which.
body:
Every few months, feature phones quietly trend again, and the reason is almost never nostalgia. It is a parent who wants big buttons and a loud speaker. A shopkeeper who needs a second number that survives a week on standby. Or someone tired of charging a smartphone every single night. Nokia — now made by HMD — still owns this corner of the market, and two models are getting searched a lot in Pakistan right now.

Nokia 2360 Flip — the one with the SOS button (around Rs 15,499)

The Nokia 2360 Flip launched at the start of November 2026 and it leans fully into being a phone for parents and grandparents. It is a proper flip phone: a 2.8-inch screen inside, a small 1.77-inch screen outside so you can see who is calling without opening it, and — the feature that actually sells it — a dedicated SOS button. There is also "Family Assist", which lets a family member manage the phone remotely, a genuinely thoughtful touch if you are buying it for an elderly relative in another city.

One important limitation: this is a 2G-only phone. Calls and texts work fine on Pakistan's networks, which still run 2G, but there is no WhatsApp, no internet to speak of, and the camera is a basic QVGA unit with a flash. Storage is a tiny 4 MB with a memory card slot for music. The battery is 1,450 mAh and removable — in a phone this simple, with no large touchscreen or background apps, that typically means several days between charges. The price in Pakistan is currently estimated at around Rs 15,499, which is not cheap for a feature phone; you are paying for the flip design and the safety features, not raw hardware.

Nokia 235 4G — the sensible one (Rs 6,999)

If the flip is about comfort, the Nokia 235 4G is about common sense. It costs Rs 6,999 in Pakistan, connects to 4G (useful as networks slowly move away from older standards), and covers the basics properly: a 2.8-inch screen, wireless FM radio, an MP3 player, Bluetooth 5.0, a 2 MP camera with flash, USB-C charging — yes, the same cable as your smartphone — and a removable 1,450 mAh battery. It runs Nokia's Series 30+ software, which your father has probably used before and will not need you to explain.

A refreshed Nokia 235 4G (2026) has also been announced, adding a small front camera for video calls. Its Pakistan price is not confirmed yet; when it lands, expect it to sit a little above the current model. If you need a phone today, the existing 235 4G at Rs 6,999 is the one to buy.

So, which one?

Buying for an elderly parent and want the safety net? The 2360 Flip, if the budget stretches. Buying a second phone, a backup for load-shedding hours, or something for the kids that is not a smartphone? The 235 4G at half the price is the smarter purchase. Either way, buy from a shop that gives you the official warranty — inexpensive feature phones are frequently copied, and a warranty is the easiest way to tell a genuine unit from a replica.

Frequently asked questions

Do these phones support WhatsApp?

No. Both are voice-and-text phones running feature-phone software: calling, SMS, FM radio and music playback are the intended uses. Smartphone applications such as WhatsApp are not supported, which is precisely why many buyers choose them for parents or as a second phone.

Will a 2G phone still work in Pakistan?

Yes. Pakistan's mobile networks continue to operate 2G services, so the 2360 Flip works normally for calls and text messages. It cannot use mobile data in any meaningful way; if you want a feature phone with 4G for future-proofing, the 235 4G is the safer purchase.

Which one is better for an elderly parent?

The 2360 Flip, if the budget allows: the flip design, external screen, SOS button and Family Assist remote management are all aimed at that use. The 235 4G is the better value for everyone else.

title: Best Smartphones Under $200 (2026): Eight Phones That Don't Feel Cheap
desc: Two hundred dollars used to buy compromise. In 2026 it buys AMOLED screens, 120Hz refresh rates and 7,000 mAh batteries. These are the eight best smartphones under $200 right now, with prices and clear verdicts.
body:
Something shifted in the last two years. The under-$200 shelf — once the home of laggy screens and cameras you apologised for — now holds phones with AMOLED displays, fast charging and chipsets that handle real games. If your budget is $200 (roughly Rs 55,000 in Pakistan), you are not settling any more. You are shopping. Here is how we would spend it.

The eight worth your money

PhonePriceWhy it makes the list
Tecno Spark 30 Pro$150AMOLED 120Hz screen at a silly price
Infinix Hot 40 Pro$163Helio G99 gaming on a budget
Redmi 13$163108 MP camera with real autofocus
Vivo Y28$1706,000 mAh battery, 44W charging
Samsung Galaxy A07$173The Samsung badge without the tax
Tecno Pova 6 Neo$1817,000 mAh and a 120Hz screen
Infinix Note 50s 5G$1815G and a 144Hz AMOLED
Redmi Note 13$192The complete package, AMOLED 120Hz

Start with the screen: Spark 30 Pro and Note 13

The Tecno Spark 30 Pro at $150 is the deal we keep coming back to. Its AMOLED panel runs at 120Hz and gets properly bright, which no LCD phone at this price can match for contrast. Spend a little more and the Redmi Note 13 at $192 answers with its own 120Hz AMOLED, a Snapdragon 685, a 108 MP camera plus an ultrawide, and 33W charging advertised to reach 50% in about 29 minutes. It is the most complete specification here if you can stretch to the top of the budget.

Gamers and battery hunters

For games, the Infinix Hot 40 Pro ($163) pairs the Helio G99 with up to 12 GB of RAM — the strongest gaming specification in this group. For battery, two phones stand apart: the Tecno Pova 6 Neo ($181) packs a 7,000 mAh cell behind a 120Hz screen, and the Vivo Y28 ($170) counters with 6,000 mAh but much faster 44W charging. Pova for days away from a socket; Y28 if a quick top-up fits your routine better.

The safe and the smart

The Samsung Galaxy A07 ($173) is for buyers who value the brand's service network and software — and with a Helio G99 inside, it is not even slow any more. The Redmi 13 ($163) is the camera pick, because its 108 MP sensor has real PDAF autofocus, the thing budget cameras usually fake. And if you keep phones for years, the Infinix Note 50s 5G ($181) is the future-proofing play: a 4 nm Dimensity 7300 chip, a 144Hz AMOLED and the only 5G radio on this page.

One warning before you check out

At this end of the market, the variant matters more than the model. Several of these phones ship in 4 GB and 8 GB RAM versions that look identical in photos. Always confirm the exact RAM and storage you are paying for, and in Pakistan, buy the PTA-approved version with warranty. Compare any two of these side by side in our comparison tool, or browse the full under $200 list.

Frequently asked questions

Why are the dollar prices different from the Pakistani prices?

The dollar figures are the phones' international prices. Pakistani retail prices also reflect import costs, PTA approval and local warranty, so the rupee figure is rarely a simple conversion — each phone's page on this site shows both.

Does the variant matter at this price?

More than the model does. Several phones in this list are sold with 4 GB, 6 GB or 8 GB of RAM at different prices, and the cheapest quote in a shop is usually for the smallest variant. Confirm the exact RAM and storage before paying.

title: Best Battery Phones in Pakistan (2026): Big Batteries That Actually Last
desc: From an 8,800 mAh Huawei to a 7,000 mAh phone under Rs 50,000 — the best battery phones on sale in Pakistan in 2026, ranked by real battery size with prices, charging speeds and honest advice.
body:
In Pakistan, battery life is rarely a secondary concern. Load-shedding, long commutes and phones that double as work tools mean battery capacity and charging speed decide many purchases. The good news: 2026 is the year big batteries went mainstream. Silicon-carbon cells have pushed capacities that would have sounded fake two years ago into ordinary phones. Here is the honest ranking from the models we track.

The biggest batteries you can buy

PhoneBatteryPrice in Pakistan
Huawei Enjoy 100 Pro Max8,800 mAhRs 82,999 (expected)
vivo Y5008,100 mAhRs 89,999
vivo Y31d7,200 mAhRs 72,999
Tecno Pova 6 Neo7,000 mAhRs 49,999
Realme C100i7,000 mAhRs 42,999
Vivo Y286,000 mAhRs 46,999

Read this before you chase the biggest number

Battery size is only half the story. A frugal chipset on a huge battery outlasts a power-hungry one, and charging speed decides how painful a low battery actually is. That is why the Vivo Y28 stays on this list despite "only" 6,000 mAh: its 44W charging is fast for this class, so it recovers charge quickly whenever a socket is available. The Tecno Pova 6 Neo is the balanced pick under Rs 50,000 — 7,000 mAh, 33W charging, a big 120Hz screen and a proper Helio G99 Ultimate chip, so the phone does not feel slow while it refuses to die.

At the top of the table, the Huawei Enjoy 100 Pro Max and its 8,800 mAh battery come with fine print: the price is expected, not official, and Huawei's HarmonyOS means no built-in Google apps (we explain this in our Enjoy 100 post). If you want maximum battery with zero software drama, vivo's Y500 (8,100 mAh) and Y31d (7,200 mAh) are the straightforward choices, priced at Rs 89,999 and Rs 72,999.

On a budget? Start under Rs 50,000

The Realme C100i at Rs 42,999 with a 7,000 mAh battery is the cheapest way into the big-battery club — just know its Unisoc chipset is built for calls, messages and light apps, not gaming. The Y28 and Pova 6 Neo above cost a little more and are far better all-round phones. And if your real problem is a phone dying by evening rather than lasting two days, anything at 6,000 mAh or above with 33W or faster charging will matter more in daily use than a further 1,000 mAh on paper.

See the full ranked list on our best battery phones page, and check any model's full specifications before you buy. A note on method: this ranking is based on published battery capacity and charging specifications. Real-world endurance also depends on the chipset, screen and software, and will vary between users.

Frequently asked questions

Does a bigger battery always last longer?

Not automatically. Capacity is the starting point, but an efficient chipset and a modest screen can make a 6,000 mAh phone outlast a poorly optimised 7,000 mAh one. Treat the figures here as a guide to potential endurance, not a guaranteed number of hours.

What is a silicon-carbon battery?

A newer battery technology that fits more capacity into a similar physical volume than conventional lithium-ion cells. It is the main reason mainstream phones above 7,000 mAh — such as the Enjoy 100 Pro Max and vivo Y500 in the table above — have become possible.

title: Samsung Galaxy S20 5G in 2026: Price in Pakistan and Whether It Is Still Worth Buying
desc: The Galaxy S20 5G was a 2020 flagship with a screen that still shames new phones. Six years on, with an estimated price of Rs 107,999 in Pakistan, should you buy one — or walk past it? The trade-offs, weighed up.
body:
People keep searching for the Galaxy S20 5G, and it is easy to see why. This was Samsung's 2020 flagship — part of the generation that brought 120Hz screens to flagship phones — and on the used market it looks like a bargain next to new mid-range phones. But a six-year-old flagship is a different animal from a new phone at the same price. Let us be straight about both sides.

Price in Pakistan

We list the Samsung Galaxy S20 5G at an estimated Rs 107,999 in Pakistan. Read that word carefully: estimated. This phone is no longer sold new through official channels, so real prices depend entirely on condition, variant and whether the unit is PTA approved. A worn, non-PTA unit should cost far less; a clean approved one commands a premium precisely because so few survive in good shape. Never pay the estimate for a phone you have not held in your hand.

What is still genuinely good

The screen. A 6.2-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X panel at 1440 x 3200 resolution with 120Hz is, even in 2026, sharper and richer than what most new phones under Rs 150,000 offer. The build is proper flagship stuff — Gorilla Glass 6 front and back, aluminium frame — and the 12 MP main camera with optical stabilisation still takes photos that hold up, especially in good light. Stereo speakers and an ultrasonic fingerprint reader round out a package that reminds you what flagships used to include by default.

What has aged — and it matters

Software support has ended; the S20 5G stops at Android 13, so it receives no newer features, and some applications may eventually raise their minimum Android version beyond it. The Exynos 990 inside the global version drew criticism at launch for running warm and throttling under sustained load, and six years have not improved it. The 4,000 mAh battery is the weakest point: modest when new, it will have lost real capacity on any used unit, so heavy users should expect frequent top-ups — or budget for a replacement battery. There is no official warranty on any unit you buy now, full stop.

Our verdict

Buy it if you are an enthusiast who found a clean, PTA-approved unit at a price that reflects its age, and you value that screen and camera over everything else. Everyone else — and we mean this kindly — is better served by a new phone with a warranty, current software and a fresh battery. Something like the Redmi Note 13 gives you a 120Hz AMOLED and current software support for less money, even if it cannot match the S20's build. Our guide to the best smartphones under $200 covers the current alternatives in more detail. Old flagships are a hobby. Buy them with your eyes open.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Galaxy S20 5G still receiving updates?

No. Its final major version is Android 13 with One UI 5.1, and Samsung has ended software support for the S20 series. The phone works normally today, but it should be bought with that limitation understood.

Is the Galaxy S20 5G PTA approved in Pakistan?

It depends entirely on the individual unit, since none are sold new through official channels any more. Check the phone's IMEI status before paying — a non-approved unit will not work on Pakistani networks, and that should be reflected in a much lower price.

title: Redmi 13 Price in Pakistan (Rs 44,999): Full Specs and Who Should Actually Buy It
desc: The Redmi 13 sells on one number: 108 megapixels. At Rs 44,999 in Pakistan, is the camera the real story, or should your money go elsewhere? Full specs, honest strengths and weaknesses, and the alternatives to consider.
body:
The Redmi 13's marketing leads with one number: 108 megapixels. It is a genuinely relevant specification on this phone, but it is not the whole story. Here is the complete picture for the Rs 44,999 the Redmi 13 costs in Pakistan, including the compromises the marketing leaves out.

The specs that matter

Display6.79-inch IPS LCD, 90Hz
ChipsetMediaTek Helio G91 Ultra
RAM / Storage6 or 8 GB / 128 or 256 GB (microSD via shared SIM slot)
Main camera108 MP with PDAF + 2 MP macro
Selfie camera13 MP
Battery5,030 mAh, 33W charging
Price in PakistanRs 44,999

The camera: genuinely good, with one honest footnote

Here is the thing most listings will not tell you: megapixels are not what makes this camera good — autofocus is. The 108 MP sensor has PDAF, so it locks onto subjects quickly and accurately, and in daylight the detail is a clear step above the 50 MP cameras most rivals offer at this price. For photographing products for your shop, documents, or family events, it is one of the stronger camera options under Rs 50,000. The footnote: that 2 MP macro camera is decoration, and night photos are average. Judge it as a strong single camera, not a versatile system.

Where it compromises

Storage is eMMC 5.1, the slower standard, so installing big apps and copying files takes noticeably longer than on UFS phones. The screen is a 90Hz LCD — perfectly decent, but rivals offer 120Hz, and one (the Tecno Spark 30 Pro) gives you AMOLED for less money. And the Helio G91 Ultra is a daily-driver chip, not a gaming one; light games run well, heavy titles need lowered settings. None of these are deal-breakers at Rs 44,999. All of them are worth knowing before you are standing at the counter.

So who should buy it?

Camera-first buyers on a budget: yes, this is your phone. Parents buying for a student who photographs notes and everything else: also yes. Gamers: the Infinix Hot 40 Pro at the same price was built for you instead. Screen snobs: look at the Spark 30 Pro. The Redmi 13 does not try to be everything, which makes the recommendation straightforward: it suits a specific buyer well. It also appears in our guide to the best phones under Rs 50,000 in Pakistan, where it is compared with its closest rivals.

title: iPad mini OLED (2026) Price in Pakistan: What the New Screen and A20 Pro Chip Cost You
desc: Apple's iPad mini finally went OLED in 2026, with the A20 Pro chip and an 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display. Here is the estimated price in Pakistan (Rs 192,999), the full specs and who this little tablet is really for.
body:
The iPad mini has always been the iPad for people who find iPads too big — readers, travellers, pilots, students who take notes in cramped lecture halls. In 2026 it got the upgrade owners had been requesting for years: an OLED screen. If you have been searching for its price in Pakistan, here it is, along with everything else that changed.

Price in Pakistan

We list the iPad mini (2026) at an estimated Rs 192,999 in Pakistan (about $698 internationally). As with most Apple products here, that is an estimate — actual shop prices vary with stock, storage variant and whether the unit is the Wi-Fi or cellular model, and early stock usually carries a premium. Storage runs 128, 256 and 512 GB.

What is new: the screen and the chip

The display is now an 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED — the same display family as Apple's Pro tablets — at 600 nits typical brightness and up to 1,200 nits in HDR. In practical terms, that means true blacks and far better contrast than the LCD panel of the previous model — a clear step up, particularly for reading and video in a dark room. Inside, the A20 Pro chip with 12 GB of RAM offers substantial performance headroom, which matters at this price because buyers tend to keep iPads for many years. The design stays delightfully small — 195.3 mm tall and just 255 g for the Wi-Fi model — and it even picks up an IP67 rating this generation.

The rest of the picture

Cameras are 12 MP front and back, the front one ultrawide for video calls. The battery is rated at 4,900 mAh with fast wired charging (about 50% in 30 minutes). Touch ID lives in the top button, the connector is USB-C, and the cellular model uses eSIM. Who should not buy it? Anyone who mainly watches video on a big screen at home (a larger, cheaper iPad serves you better) and anyone put off by estimated-price early stock — waiting a few weeks usually softens Pakistani launch prices.

Should you upgrade from the 2024 mini?

If your 2024 iPad mini still handles everything you ask of it, the only compelling reason to upgrade is the screen. For first-time mini buyers, this is the strongest version of the formula so far — just buy it from a shop that gives you a proper bill and warranty, because at Rs 192,999 you want paperwork.

Frequently asked questions

Is the iPad mini (2026) officially available in Pakistan?

Apple does not sell directly in Pakistan, so units reach the market through importers and authorised resellers. That is why the price here is listed as estimated: it varies with stock and variant, and early stock usually costs more.

Does the Wi-Fi model need PTA approval?

No — a Wi-Fi-only tablet does not connect to mobile networks and needs no registration. If you are considering the cellular model, check its DIRBS registration status before paying, since an unregistered device cannot use a Pakistani SIM or eSIM.

What is the difference from the 2024 iPad mini?

Based on the published specifications: an OLED display in place of LCD, the newer A20 Pro chip with 12 GB of RAM, an IP67 rating, and a slightly larger 8.5-inch screen. The full comparison is on the two models' specification pages.
